claim: New York City has as many students in its district schools as Colorado has in all its public schools
caveat_shown: Counting the city's roughly 150,000 charter pupils and its pre-K would put New York City ahead of Colorado rather than behind it.

claim: New York City has as many people on the city payroll as Texas has state employees
caveat_shown: Both are actual full-time headcounts. The federal survey reflects a March 2025 payroll.

claim: New York City houses as many people in public housing and its converted successors as live in Cleveland
caveat_shown: Public housing proper holds 298,206 authorised residents; another 46,455 live in developments converted to private management under PACT, which the housing authority no longer counts as public housing.

claim: New York City shelters as many homeless people each night as Andorra has people
caveat_shown: Department of Homeless Services shelters only; other agencies' shelters and migrant sites are not included.

claim: New York City has as many college students as all of Massachusetts
caveat_shown: Massachusetts is fall 2022, the latest year in the federal table; New York City's is a 2024 count.

claim: New York City employs as many public school teachers as all of Ireland
caveat_shown: Ireland's count is from 2022, the most recent its education department publishes, and it was then rising by about 2,000 a year, so Ireland has probably passed New York City since.

claim: New York City has as many people on Medicaid as all of Florida
caveat_shown: New York City's month is July 2026, Florida's April 2026.

claim: New York City has as many residents with a disability as Virginia
caveat_shown: Civilian, non-institutional population on both sides.

claim: New York City proposes to spend as much on its police department as Iraq spends on its military
caveat_shown: Executive Plan figure for fiscal 2027, not the adopted line.

claim: New York City proposes to spend as much on public schools as Iceland produces in a year
caveat_shown: Executive Plan figure for fiscal 2027.

claim: New York City takes in as much visitor spending as Tunisia's entire economy
New York City has real estate worth as much as Mexico produces in a year
caveat_shown: Department of Finance market values are the city's own estimates and lag sale prices.

claim: New York City has as many millionaires as the Bay Area
caveat_shown: The Bay Area here is San Francisco plus Silicon Valley, a region rather than a city. Both counts mean at least $1 million in liquid, investable assets.

claim: New York City has as many Wall Street jobs as Alphabet has employees worldwide
caveat_shown: New York City's figure is preliminary.

claim: New York City has a Queens whose economy is the size of Ethiopia's
caveat_shown: Holds for 2024 only. Ethiopia devalued the birr and the IMF puts its 2025 dollar GDP at $109 billion, a quarter lower, so the two have already parted company.

claim: New York City has a Staten Island whose economy is the size of Mongolia's
caveat_shown: Both figures are 2024. The IMF puts Mongolia 7 percent higher in 2025.

claim: New York City maintains as many bridges and tunnels as Rhode Island has bridges
caveat_shown: The two sides count different things: the city figure mixes bridges with tunnels, the federal figure is bridges over 20 feet on public roads, and neither includes the big Port Authority and MTA crossings.

claim: New York City has as many fire hydrants as London
caveat_shown: London's hydrants are split across four water companies; New York City's belong to one utility. Both figures are rounded.

claim: New York City has as many miles of water main as Los Angeles
New York City runs as many public buses as Hong Kong's whole franchised fleet
New York City gives as many bus rides a year as the European Union has people
caveat_shown: New York City Transit buses only; the MTA Bus Company adds about 120 million.

claim: New York City is served by airports that carry as many passengers as Istanbul's
caveat_shown: Newark is in New Jersey and Stewart is in Orange County, so this is the regional airport system rather than airports inside the city.

claim: New York City licenses as many yellow cabs as London licenses black cabs
caveat_shown: Both are licence counts. About a fifth of New York City medallions are not currently in service, so fewer yellow cabs work the streets than the cap allows.

claim: New York City runs a Staten Island Ferry that carries as many passengers as all of Sydney's
New York City draws as many museum visitors to the Met as the Uffizi draws in Florence
caveat_shown: Both are multi-site museums: the Met counts Fifth Avenue and the Cloisters, the Uffizi counts the gallery, the Pitti Palace and the Boboli Gardens.

claim: New York City fills as many Broadway seats at home as touring Broadway fills everywhere else
New York City sits at the centre of a region that speaks as many languages as Indonesia
caveat_shown: The 700-plus count covers the whole New York metropolitan area, not the five boroughs, and is a field tally of immigrant and heritage language varieties rather than a census. Indonesia's is distinct living languages.

claim: New York City has as many murders a year as Houston has homicides
caveat_shown: Houston's count is homicides reported to its police. Houston has 2.4 million people to New York City's 8.5 million, so its rate is about three times higher.

claim: New York City answers as many 911 calls a year as all of North Carolina
caveat_shown: New York City's is a fiscal year to June 2025; North Carolina's is calendar 2025.

claim: New York City makes as many arrests a year as Buffalo has people
New York City sends an ambulance as many times a year as Philadelphia has people
